output.headline: Declares district vehicles surplus so the Risk Management Department can dispose of them
output.summary: The Board is declaring certain district-owned vehicles obsolete and surplus, which allows the district to dispose of them. The official text does not list the vehicles or state any dollar amount.

output.headline: Declares district equipment surplus so the Risk Management Department can dispose of it
output.summary: The Board is declaring certain district-owned equipment obsolete and surplus, which allows the district to dispose of it. The official text does not list the equipment or state any dollar amount.

output.headline: Declares more district equipment surplus so the Risk Management Department can dispose of it
output.summary: The Board is declaring certain district-owned equipment obsolete and surplus, which allows the district to dispose of it. The official text does not list the equipment or state any dollar amount.

output.headline: Declares district warehouse vehicles surplus so the district can dispose of them
output.summary: The Board is declaring certain district warehouse vehicles obsolete and surplus, which allows the district to dispose of them. The official text does not list the vehicles or state any dollar amount.

output.headline: Moves $16,000 at Madison Park Academy from unused transportation to teacher training
output.summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, the Board moves $16,000 in Measure N funds at Madison Park Academy from transportation costs to extended teacher contracts for teacher training and assignment mastery. Transportation is not needed during distance learning. This is a transfer within the school's budget, not new spending.

output.headline: Updates East Bay Asian Youth Center's in-person learning support at Roosevelt Middle at no added cost
output.summary: The district is changing its memorandum of understanding (MOU) with East Bay Asian Youth Center to update the scope of work for in-person learning supports for grades 6-8 at Roosevelt Middle School. There is no added cost, and the cap stays at $399,538. The agreement runs August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2021.

output.headline: Hires Star Elevator for $39,435 to modify fire circuitry on Fremont High's new elevator, without bidding
output.summary: The district is hiring Star Elevator of San Carlos to modify the fire service circuitry on the passenger elevator for the Fremont High School new construction project. The price is $39,435, which includes a $2,030.33 contingency, and it was not competitively bid. Work is scheduled to run from February 11, 2021 to June 30, 2021, paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Moves $13,700 at Castlemont High from unused transportation to teacher project leads
output.summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, the Board moves $13,700 in Measure N funds at Castlemont High School from four transportation budget lines to extended teacher contracts. The teachers will serve as project leads for CastleWorks. Transportation is not needed during distance learning. This is a transfer within the school's budget, not new spending.

output.headline: Moves $50,000 at Coliseum College Prep to open a case manager position
output.summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, the Board moves $50,000 in Measure N funds at Coliseum College Preparatory Academy into clerical salaries to open a case manager position. $8,000 comes from supplies and materials and $42,000 from teacher stipends, which are needed less during distance learning. This is a transfer within the school's budget, not new spending.

output.headline: Moves $3,125 at Skyline High from substitute pay to teacher stipends for collaboration time
output.summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, the Board moves $3,125 in Measure N funds at Skyline High School from teacher substitutes to teacher stipends for extended contracts, used for collaboration and professional development time. The text expects very few staff absences. This is a transfer within the school's budget, not new spending.

output.headline: Moves $7,000 at Skyline High from conference costs to teacher stipends for collaboration time
output.summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, the Board moves $7,000 in Measure N funds at Skyline High School from conference expenses to teacher stipends for extended contracts, used for collaboration and professional development time. Travel to conferences is unlikely to be possible. This is a transfer within the school's budget, not new spending.

output.headline: Moves $5,000 at Skyline High from unused transportation to VAPA technology equipment
output.summary: The Board approves a request from Skyline High School to move $5,000 of its 2020-2021 Measure N (college and career readiness) budget. The money shifts from transportation costs, which the school says will have little impact because field trips will likely not be possible, to equipment for visual and performing arts (VAPA) technology. The Measure N Commission recommended the change.

output.headline: Moves $1,500 at Skyline High from unused conference funds to VAPA technology equipment
output.summary: The Board approves a request from Skyline High School to move $1,500 of its 2020-2021 Measure N (college and career readiness) budget. The money shifts from conference expenses, which the school says will have little impact because travel to conferences will likely not be possible, to equipment for visual and performing arts (VAPA) technology. The Measure N Commission recommended the change.

output.headline: Ends the district's third-year contract with School Innovations & Achievement on July 1, 2021
output.summary: The Board is ending Year 3 of its contract with School Innovations & Achievement for good governance and program advisory services. It is a termination for convenience, meaning the district ends it without needing a reason tied to the vendor's performance. It takes effect July 1, 2021.

output.headline: Accepts a no-cost web development course from ScriptEd (Code Nation) for virtual classes
output.summary: ScriptEd, which does business as Code Nation, will virtually teach its Intro to Web Development curriculum to students twice a week, for 45 to 60 minutes each time. The district pays nothing. The agreement runs January 1, 2021 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Accepts a no-cost career mentoring program for high school students from OverCOME
output.summary: OverCOME will match high school students from underserved or academically disadvantaged backgrounds with mentors in fields they are interested in. Mentors and students will set goals and connect to job shadowing, internships and networking. The district pays nothing, and the agreement runs December 15, 2020 through November 19, 2021.

output.headline: Updates Oakland Kids First's in-person learning support at Castlemont High at no added cost
output.summary: The district is changing its memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Oakland Kids First, which provides in-person learning supports to grade 9-12 students at Castlemont High School. Supports can include help with technology, mentoring and connecting students to other services. There is no added cost, and the cap stays at $197,238 for July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Asian Youth Center up to $91,000 for attendance support at Garfield Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $91,000.00

output.summary: East Bay Asian Youth Center will work with school staff to track attendance, identify students at risk of missing too much school, and connect students and families to community resources. It will also run monthly attendance raffles and virtual assemblies at Garfield Elementary School. The contract is capped at $91,000 for September 1, 2020 through May 28, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $10,000 for Reading Partners tutoring at Laurel Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00

output.summary: Reading Partners will provide a reading tutoring program for identified students at Laurel Elementary School. The contract is capped at $10,000 and covers August 10, 2020 through May 28, 2021. The Board is approving it after the start date, as a ratification.

output.headline: Adds $2,900 to Servio Consulting's contract to update the COVID Daily Assessment survey
output.summary: The district is adding $2,900 to its agreement with Servio Consulting, which raises the cap from $35,000 to $37,900. The company will reprogram the COVID Daily Assessment survey so later questions depend on earlier answers, across web, text and voice. The work covers September 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Pays Girls Inc. of Alameda County up to $14,093 for reading tutoring at Bridges Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $14,093.00

output.summary: Girls Inc. of Alameda County will give small-group, 30-minute tutoring sessions 2 to 4 times a week to at least 40 students at Bridges Academy @ Melrose. The students read from one month to two and a half years below grade level. The contract is capped at $14,093 for August 19, 2020 through May 27, 2021.

output.headline: Pays Girls Inc. of Alameda County up to $907 for tutoring at Bridges Academy, Aug. 10-19, 2020

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $907.00

output.summary: Girls Inc. of Alameda County will give small-group, 30-minute tutoring sessions 2 to 4 times a week to at least 40 students at Bridges Academy @ Melrose. This contract is capped at $907 and covers only August 10 through August 19, 2020, just before the term of a separate $14,093 agreement for the same work.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $18,250 for a weekly science enrichment program at Sequoia Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $18,250.00

output.summary: A contractor will provide a 30-minute weekly enriched science program to all TK-5th grade students at Sequoia Elementary School, to build interest and talent in math and science. The contract is capped at $18,250 and covers February 1, 2021 through May 14, 2021. The Board is approving it as a ratification.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $12,500 for Luna Dance Institute's inclusive dance program at Grass Valley Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $12,500.00

output.summary: Luna Dance Institute will continue building a dance program for students with and without disabilities at Grass Valley Elementary School. The contract is capped at $12,500 and covers September 1, 2020 through May 14, 2021. The Board is approving it as a ratification.

output.headline: Lets the district share student data with UC San Francisco for a school reopening study
output.summary: This data sharing agreement covers the district's transmission of student data to the University of California, San Francisco, and how the university must protect it. The data supports a study of indoor school settings in the Bay Area, looking at how well federal safe-reopening guidance works. The agreement runs January 12, 2021 through June 11, 2021.

output.headline: Accepts a $100,000 Learn Fresh Education grant for STEAM renovations at Brookfield Elementary
output.summary: Learn Fresh Education Co of Denver is giving Brookfield Elementary School $100,000 for renovations to support science, technology, engineering, art and math (STEAM) learning. The grant runs December 15, 2020 through December 15, 2021.

output.headline: Updates Safe Passages' in-person learning support at United for Success Academy at no added cost
output.summary: The district is changing its memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Safe Passages, which provides in-person learning supports to grade 6-8 students at United for Success Academy. Supports include help with technology, mentoring and connecting students to other services. There is no added cost, and the cap stays at $192,343 for August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2021.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Asian Youth Center up to $45,000 for virtual student support at Edna Brewer Middle

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $45,000.00

output.summary: East Bay Asian Youth Center will provide 177 days of virtual wellness check-ins, academic support, enrichment and case management for students at Edna Brewer Middle School. Services are one-on-one and in small groups over Zoom. The contract is capped at $45,000 for August 10, 2020 through May 28, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $19,500 for Higher Gliffs to lead a student mural project at Fremont High

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $19,500.00

output.summary: Higher Gliffs will provide a community muralist and artist-in-residence to work with Fremont High School visual art students on a mural about the school's history. The mural is to be painted in the Fremont Auditorium the following year. The contract is capped at $19,500 and covers January 4, 2021 through May 27, 2021. The Board is approving it as a ratification.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $3,200 for Inner-City Bliss to teach meditation at Dewey Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $3,200.00

output.summary: Inner-City Bliss will teach a 16-week program of beginner to advanced meditation to Dewey Academy students. It supports health education standards for career technical education. The contract is capped at $3,200 and covers February 1, 2021 through May 27, 2021. The Board is approving it as a ratification.

output.headline: Lets the district share data with the University of Delaware for a no-cost curriculum study
output.summary: This data sharing agreement lets the district share data with the University of Delaware, which will run a no-cost research study on how best to support high-quality curricula in the district. The agreement runs January 8, 2021 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Extends the WestEd science standards grant to March 31, 2021 with no change to its $501,930
output.summary: The district and WestEd are extending a grant that supports the California Next Generation Science Standards K-8 Early Implementation Initiative for Years 5 and 6. The end date moves to March 31, 2021. The amount stays at $501,930, and all other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Carries over $1,831,416.23 in unspent 2019-2020 Measure N funds for named district and charter schools
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution letting district and charter schools carry unspent 2019-2020 Measure N (college and career readiness) funds into the next year. The cumulative amount is $1,831,416.23. The text does not list the individual schools or how each will use its share.

output.headline: Awards Common Vision up to $864,000 to deliver district meals and produce boxes to homes

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $864,000.00

output.summary: The Board awards a bid to Common Vision of Berkeley to deliver district-prepared meals and produce boxes to students' homes. The contract is capped at $864,000 and runs from February 15, 2021 through June 30, 2021. Common Vision was chosen as the responsive, responsible bidder.

output.headline: Carries over $20,123.97 in unspent 2019-2020 Measure G1 funds for named district middle schools
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution, recommended by the Measure G1 oversight commission, letting named district middle schools carry unspent 2019-2020 Measure G1 (teacher retention and middle school improvement) funds into the next year and approving their plans for the money. The cumulative amount is $20,123.97. The text does not list the individual schools.
